name: elfutils
desc: Libraries and utilities for handling ELF objects
why: Libraries and tools for ELF internals open a door into how binaries are actually laid out, though it is widely used plumbing.

brief.what_it_is: elfutils is a collection of utilities and libraries to read, create and modify ELF binary files, and to find and handle DWARF debug data, symbols, thread state and stacktraces for processes and core files on GNU/Linux. It has three libraries: libelf (read, modify and create ELF files), libdw (read DWARF, find separate debuginfo, symbols and inspect process state), and libasm (assemble and disassemble instructions). It also ships about 20 eu-* command-line tools, such as eu-readelf, eu-nm, eu-objdump, eu-strip, eu-unstrip, eu-stack and eu-addr2line. The tools take ELF files, DWARF data, processes or core files as input and print information or write modified or created ELF files and archives.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes the project as a collection of utilities and libraries for reading, creating and modifying ELF binaries and for handling DWARF debug data, symbols, thread state and stacktraces. It gives no separate motivation statement.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage describes the layers without going into implementation. Three libraries (libelf, libdw, libasm) provide the ELF, DWARF and assembly functions, and the eu-* utilities are built on them. Machine-specific handling lives in per-architecture backends, listed as aarch64, arm, bpf, i386, ppc64, riscv64, s390x, x86_64 and about a dozen others.

commands_seen.context: Homepage's stated way to check out the current elfutils source code from sourceware.org.

brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no build or install steps beyond the git clone of the source tree; release tarballs (tar.bz2, with signatures) are on the sourceware FTP area. It mentions no runtimes, accounts or first-run configuration. The package list supplied with this entry includes both elfutils-* and eu-* executable names for each tool.
brief.standout: One package covers ELF editing (eu-strip, eu-elfcompress, eu-ar), DWARF and symbol reading, and live stack inspection of processes and core files (eu-stack). Its eu-unstrip and eu-make-debug-archive tools tie stripped binaries to separate debug information and offline debugging archives, which the homepage emphasizes.
brief.status: Appears maintained. The homepage lists 0.197 as the latest release, followed by a long run of earlier releases, and points to a current git tree, a bug tracker and a development mailing list. The homepage gives no release date or last-commit date, so the exact recency is unknown. The page is served from the old fedorahosted.org address and mentions a newer debuginfod client/server.
brief.caveats: The homepage describes the tools as GNU/Linux-focused. libasm has only partial support, for i686 and BPF instructions. Licensing is mixed: libraries and backends are dual GPLv2+/LGPLv3+, and the utilities are GPLv3+. The homepage uses the legacy fedorahosted.org address. Brew caveats were empty, and I did not check build requirements.
quotes: elfutils is a collection of utilities and libraries to read, create and modify ELF binary files, find and handle DWARF debug data, symbols, thread state and stacktraces for processes and core files on GNU/Linux.
eu-elflint: Pedantic checking of ELF files compliance with gABI/psABI spec.
eu-make-debug-archive: Script to make an offline archive for debugging of ELF binaries and linux kernel modules
fetch_log: https://fedorahosted.org/elfutils/ - fetched OK; homepage is not a GitHub repo and contained the full project description, so I did not follow further links.
